inputs.original_text: They’ve convicted Father Bernard Domini under France’s new “psychological subjection” law—a vague tool that can be turned against religious communities whenever they become inconvenient. The alarm from civil-liberties advocates is no surprise: this looks less like neutral law enforcement and more like institutions testing how far they can stretch the rules to silence dissent.
inputs.modified_text: They convicted Father Bernard Domini under France’s new “psychological subjection” law, and the vagueness is the point: it gives institutions room to brand inconvenient religious communities a threat. The civil-liberties alarm is a warning that this may be a test run—stretch the law against one dissenting group, then normalize using it to silence others.
